newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates edge down at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates edge down at close.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down five basis points at 24.75 percent when dealers took profits in late trade after rates had gained during much of the session, traders said.
Overnight rates reached a high of 26 percent on expectations that primary rates were about to soar in reaction to liquidity pressures in the secondary market and to shore up the weak peso.
Traders said they thought the market had overreacted to the prospect of primary rate hikes, however.
"Dealers panicked and began to sell paper at any price. The market is overeacting and abrupt hikes in primary rates could trigger more uncertainty rather than shore up the peso," he added.
"Banco de Mexico's announcement yesterday heated up the market too much, and led to forecasts that primary rates would gain by at almost 400 basis points," said a trader.
Banco de Mexixco announced yesterday that it would allow the money market to close with a liquidity shortfall of 20 million pesos, rather than zero, as had been the case since August 16.
Term rates climbed in line with expected primary rate hikes. Cetes 28-day rates closed at 26.50 percent, compared to last week's auction rate of 22.74 percent.
A Reuters survey of 11 money market traders showed they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to rise by an average of 371 basis points to 26.45 percent.
Some traders felt that Secondary rates gained sharply due to speculation and market overrection to liquidity pressures and weakness in the peso.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed earlier 1.1 centavos weaker 7.7190/7.7290.
vernight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 150 basis points at 27.50 percent.
Total credit maturities for Wednesday were estimated at 6.116 billion pesos.
